params.body:
Netwerk and Verkennen were slow on every click, gave no sign they were working, and the 3D graph looked flat and zoomed in too far on a click. Measured on a local database of production size (4,933 relations, 9,700 links, 7,600 bookings).

## Fetch less, and only when it changes

| Page | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Netwerk (any tab, or opening a relation) | 620 to 750 ms | 46 to 150 ms |
| Verkennen (any type) | 440 to 470 ms | 95 to 137 ms |
| A click on Netwerk (Livewire) | 750 ms | 115 ms |

- **`Network::contacts()`** loaded every relation and link as an Eloquent model with dates cast, on every request: 629 ms on its own. It now reads plain rows with only the columns it needs, and only the relations that appear: 51 ms. The result is cached until the next `relations:sync`, keyed on that command's `LAST` stamp: 15 ms. Tags are read fresh on every call, so a tag saved at the table shows at once.
- **Revenue and quotes-to-orders** are cached the same way. The cache only stores plain arrays (`cache.serializable_classes` is off), so the revenue rows go in as arrays and come back as the objects the view reads.
- **Verkennen** read all records twice per request (once for the list, once for the counts on the left); it now reads them once (`allRows`). Bookings are read as plain rows instead of models, sorted with one `usort`, and the week summary parses each date once instead of once per row.

## Something shows while it loads

A thin green bar along the top of the page (`resources/js/busy.js`) shows on every Livewire request and when a link or form leaves for another page. It waits 150 ms, so quick answers do not flicker, and it skips CSV and printout links. It is in every layout, the site app included.

## 3D

- **Depth.** Switching from 2D kept every dot at depth 0, so the 3D view was the 2D picture on a plane. Dots now get a depth derived from their id (stable across loads) and the layout settles in full before it is fitted. Measured on the sample: depth spread 55 against 78 in width, where it was 0.
- **Clicking.** A click moved the camera to 120 units from the dot. It now turns to the dot from where the camera is and keeps the distance (at least 260). The zoom buttons zoom towards what the camera looks at, not towards the origin. In 2D, a click centres the dot and zooms in only up to 1.2.
- Names in 3D are larger.

## A bug from #70

The selection was part of the graph's `x-data` attribute. A click selects a relation, the attribute changed, and Alpine restarted the whole graph on every click. The graph now reads the selection from `$wire.selected` and follows it with `$watch`.

## Tests

- `NetworkTest`: counts are kept until the next sync while a tag shows at once; a new sync stamp counts again. 13 tests.
- Full suite 229 + 1 green, JS 13/13, pint clean.
- In headless Chromium on the production-size database: the timings above; the bar shows during a slowed Livewire request and is gone after it; in 3D a click keeps the camera distance (687 before, 673 after); no page or server errors.
